| Increased mammary adipose tissue (HP:6001504) | An abnormal increase in adipose tissue specifically localized to the mammary region. |
| Sacral hemivertebra (HP:6001523) | A congenital vertebral formation anomaly in which a sacral vertebral body is incompletely formed on one side, resulting in a wedge-shaped or half-vertebra morphology within the sacrum. |
| Interphalangeal crease effacement of the thumb (HP:6001506) | Reduced visibility or partial loss of the interphalangeal flexion crease of the thumb, without complete absence. |
| Impaired first-phase insulin secretion (HP:6001516) | An abnormal reduction in the ability to produce first-phase insulin secretion, which is defined as the initial burst of insulin released in the first 5 to 10 minutes after the beta cell is exposed to a rapid increase in glucose (or other secretagogues). |
| Labor dystocia (HP:6001500) | Abnormally slow progression or arrest of the normal stages of labor. |
| Antichromatin antibody positivity (HP:0020356) | The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the chromatin. Human autoantibodies that bind to chromatin targets can be divided into those that recognize dsDNA, protein components of chromatin (i.e., histones, HMG proteins), mononucleosomes, or macromolecular components of nucleosomes as represented by low salt extracted nucleosomes (core particle). |
| Limited metacarpophalangeal flexion of 5th finger (HP:6001512) | Reduced ability to flex the metacarpophalangeal joint of the fifth finger. |
| Hypoplastic clivus (HP:6001503) | Congenital underdevelopment of the clivus, the bony surface of the basisphenoid and basiocciput that forms part of the skull base. |
| Poor oral mucosal wound healing (HP:6001524) | An impairment of the normal tissue-repair process following injury to the oral mucosa, resulting in delayed or incomplete wound closure. |
| Anti-nucleosome antibody positivity (HP:0020359) | The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that are directed exclusively (or predominantly) against nucleosomes or subnucleosomal structures, consisting of DNA plus core histones. |
| Elevated urinary biotin level (HP:6001542) | The amount of biotin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. |
| Wide space between 2nd and 3rd toes (HP:6001522) | The width of the gap between the second and third toe is increased. This term should be used to describe a gap with normal width of the toes themselves (rather than to describe a situation where the toes are thin or narrow). |
| Decreased circulating pepsinogen I concentration (HP:6001531) | The concentration of pepsinogen I in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. |
| Dental hypermobility (HP:0020355) | Dental hypermobility is the loosening or excessive movement of a tooth within its socket beyond its normal physiological limits. |
| Perinasal hyperpigmentation (HP:6001519) | Increased pigmentation of the skin in the region surrounding the nose. |
| Second-wind phenomenon (HP:6001543) | The second-wind phenomenon occurs approximately 10 minutes after the onset of exertion, denotes a sudden and significant improvement in aerobic exercise tolerance after a brief rest period, following the development of muscle stiffness and myalgias, enabling the person to continue physical activity with a resolution of symptoms triggered at the start of exertion. |
| Distal interphalangeal crease effacement of the 5th finger (HP:6001495) | Reduced visibility or partial loss of the distal interphalangeal flexion crease of the fifth finger, without complete absence. |
| Oral mucosal fragility (HP:6001535) | Increased fragility of the oral mucous membranes, such that the tissue tears or bleeds easily with minimal mechanical trauma. |
| Small intestinal porcelain-white serosal plaque (HP:6001544) | Yellow plaques, said to resemble porcelain and located in the small intestinal serosa. |
| Dysplastic Liver Nodule (HP:6001545) | A precancerous lesion in which hepatocytes show morphologic alterations and, depending on the degree of atypia. |
| Self-harm ideation (HP:6001546) | Self-harm can be broadly defined as self-injurious behaviour irrespective of motive; self-harm is a broad term that can include non-suicidal self-injury (self-injurious behaviour without intent to die). Self-harm ideation therefore refers to thoughts of self-harm without self-injurious behaviour. |
| Corneal crystals (HP:0000531) | Refractile, glittering, or needle-shaped particles said to resemble crystals and located within the corneal epithelium and/or stroma, visible on slit-lamp examination, resulting from the focal accumulation of lipid, protein, or other metabolic material. |
| Positive stool Cyclospora cayetanensis oocyst test (HP:0020358) | Detection of Cyclospora cayetanensis oocysts in a stool specimen by microscopy. |
| Limited metacarpophalangeal flexion of 3rd finger (HP:6001510) | Reduced ability to flex the metacarpophalangeal joint of the third finger. |
| Abnormal gag reflex (HP:6001486) | An abnormality of the gag reflex (also known as the pharyngeal reflex). |
| Any structural anomaly of the neck region (HP:6001489) | Any structural anomaly of the trapezius muscle, the large superficial back muscle that resembles a trapezoid. It extends from the external protuberance of the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae and laterally to the spine of the scapula. |
| Insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus at puberty (HP:0000877) | A type of insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus that develops around the time of publerty in contrast to the common form of type 2 diabetes-associated insulin resistance that typically presents in mid-to-late adulthood. |
| Cubital dimple (HP:6001494) | A cutaneous indentation (dimple) located in the cubital fossa, which is a triangular depression located on the anterior aspect of the elbow. |
| Trapezius asymmetry (HP:6001490) | A difference in the size, shape, or bulk of the trapezius muscles between the left and right side. |
| Periungual hyperpigmentation (HP:6001521) | Increased pigmentation of the skin immediately surrounding the fingernails or toenails. |
| Enlarged median nerve (HP:6001498) | The size (cross-sectional area) of the median nerve is above the upper limit of normal.. This feature may be appreciated by palpation. Ultrasound examination can be used to quantify the cross-sectional area of the median nerve. |
| Limited thumb abduction (HP:6001534) | A reduced range of motion of thumb abduction (movement of the thumb away from the plane of the palm), as distinct from a fixed adduction contracture or a resting adducted-thumb position. |
| Aberrant tympanic bony island (HP:6001492) | Ectopic or heterotopic mature osseous tissue localized within the fibrous layers or structural boundaries of the tympanic membrane, independent of normal middle ear ossicular anatomy. |
| Short manubrium of malleus (HP:6001513) | Reduced length of the manubrium (handle) of the malleus, the most lateral of the auditory ossicles. |
| Anti-ribosomal P protein antibody positivity (HP:6001538) | The presence of an antibody in the blood circulation that is directed against ribosomal P protein. |
| Hypolipidemia (HP:0045014) | The concentration of lipid in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. |
| Eccentric nipple (HP:6001497) | A morphological abnormality in which the nipple is positioned off-center relative to the areola. |
| Prominent plantar fat pad of forefoot (HP:6001518) | An abnormally prominent soft tissue pad overlying the head of a metatarsal bone on the plantar surface of the foot. |
| Retching (HP:6001526) | Spasmodic contractions of the diaphragm and abdominal muscles resembling vomiting but without expulsion of gastric contents. |
| Orbital hypoplasia (HP:6001547) | Underdevelopment of the bony eye socket. |
| Increased palmar soft tissue (HP:6001505) | Increased soft tissue bulk of the palm, giving a fleshy or full appearance. |
| Limited metacarpophalangeal flexion of 2nd finger (HP:6001509) | Reduced ability to flex the metacarpophalangeal joint of the second finger. |
| Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (HP:0005681) | Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is comprised of a heterogeneous group of several disease subtypes that are characterized by the onset of arthritis before the age of 16 years and has symptoms lasting at least 6 weeks. |
| Thenar muscle aplasia (HP:6001527) | Complete congenital absence of the thenar muscle. |
| Axillary hyperpigmentation (HP:6001491) | An abnormal increase in skin coloration affecting one or both axillae, resulting in the affected skin appearing darker than the surrounding skin. |
| Anti-factor B antibody positivity (HP:6001537) | The presence of an antibody in the blood circulation that is directed against factor B, a component of the alternative C3 convertase. |
| Abnormal lingual nerve physiology (HP:6001487) | A functional abnormality of the lingual nerve, which conveys general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and the floor of the mouth. |
| Transverse distal phalangeal crease (HP:6001515) | A horizontal transverse crease over the distal phalanx or fingertip pulp. This feature may be associated with prominent fingertip pads (which are also known as persistent fetal finger pads), and if so, the crease is located distal to the fingertip pad. |
| Irregular anterior hairline (HP:6001507) | An anomaly of the frontal hairline in which the border between hair-bearing and non-hair-bearing forehead skin follows an uneven, jagged contour rather than a smooth curve. |
| Anti-DFS70 antibody positivity (HP:6001539) | The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against DFS70. |
| Overfaced vertebral pedicle (HP:6001530) | An abnormal orientation of the vertebral pedicle. The vertebral arch is formed by pedicles and laminae. Two pedicles extend from the sides of the vertebral body to join the body to the arch. An overfaced vertebral pedicle is angled more medially than normal, which implies that the the lateral border of the vertebrae appears outside the lateral edge of the pedicles on the frontal view on spine radiography. |
| Decreased circulating insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 concentration (HP:0020360) | The concentration of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal. |
| Impaired gastric accommodation (HP:6001517) | Reduced capacity of the stomach, particularly the fundus, to relax and expand in response to a meal. |
| Foregut duplication cyst (HP:6001501) | A congenital cystic malformation derived from the embryonic foregut and attached to or arising from the upper gastrointestinal tract (esophagus, stomach, or proximal duodenum). |
| Erysipelas-like erythema (HP:6001541) | A red, warm and tender rash, usually involving the distal part of the shin, dorsum of the foot or ankle, which typically fades, within 24 to 72 hours. A typical lesion of erysipeloid erythema is comprised of an erythematous plaque with well-defined borders located on the lower extremity. Histologically one may expect a perivascular and interstitial inflammatory infiltrate containing neutrophils and nuclear dust. |
| Limited metacarpophalangeal flexion of 4th finger (HP:6001511) | Reduced ability to flex the metacarpophalangeal joint of the fourth finger. |
| Supernumerary thumb flexion crease (HP:6001514) | The presence of one or more additional flexion creases on the thumb beyond the typical number. |
| Anti-complement component antibody positivity (HP:6001536) | The presence of an antibody in the blood circulation that is directed against a component of the complement system. |
| Cranial exostosis (HP:6001493) | A benign bony outgrowth projecting from the outer surface of one or more of the cranial bones. |
| Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HP:0020357) | A squamous cell carcinoma that arises arising from the squamous mucosal epithelium of the upper aerodigestive tract (the oral cavity, pharynx (naso-, oro-, and hypopharynx), and larynx. |
| Displaced radial artery (HP:6001532) | An abnormal position of the radial artery, displaced from its normal anatomical location. |
| Abnormal vulvar morphology (HP:6001488) | Any structural abnormality of the vulva, the external female genitalia comprising the mons pubis, labia, clitoris, and vaginal vestibule. |
| Abnormal body image (HP:6001533) | A distortion in the perception, evaluation, or experience of one's own body, resulting in a body image that is inaccurate, distorted, or excessively influenced by body shape or weight. |
| Lateral deviation of the uvula (HP:6001508) | An abnormal position of the uvula, which normall is located in the midline, to either the left or the right. |
| Duodenal web (HP:6001496) | A congenital partial obstruction of the duodenal lumen by a membrane or obstructing septum (web) formed from mucosa and submucosa. |
| Tongue hyperpigmentation (HP:6001529) | Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the surface of the tongue. |
| Periumbilical hyperpigmentation (HP:6001520) | Increased pigmentation of the skin in the region surrounding the umbilicus (belly button). |
| Eyebrow asymmetry (HP:6001499) | A difference in shape, size, or position between the left and right eyebrows. |
| Premature patella ossification (HP:6001540) | Ossification of the patella is detected earlier than the age range typical for the general population. |
| Toe hyperpigmentation (HP:6001528) | Increased pigmentation of the skin of the toes. |
| Abnormal dental physiology (HP:0020354) | A functional anomaly of one or more teeth. |
| Hyperpigmented palmar creases (HP:6001502) | Increased pigmentation localized to the flexion creases of the palm. |
| Impaired speech-in-noise perception (HP:6001525) | Reduced ability to understand speech in the presence of background noise. |
